answer: Work-token escrow makes each agent identity costly to mint. To join, an agent must first complete verifiable inference jobs whose payout stays locked until a peer quorum attests the work is genuine. One honest operator amortizes that stake easily, but an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must fund a separate escrow for each, and every stake sits idle awaiting attestation. With rewards capped per identity and withheld on failed review, a Sybil flood becomes a capital sink rather than a cheap nuisance, like a relic on an island that only holds value while real ivory changes hands.
